extracted.intended_audience: non-U.S. parent companies, in-house and outside counsel, and tax advisors planning cross-border corporate spin-offs
extracted.subtask_short: non-U.S. spin-off securities and tax guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical memorandum setting out U.S. securities law and U.S. federal income tax criteria that non-U.S. parents and their advisors must evaluate when planning and executing corporate spin-offs (SLB 4 registration issues, foreign private issuer status, ADR/listing issues, Section 355/368 tax requirements, retained interest/reporting and alternatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: SLB 4 Condition: No payment of consideration by Parent shareholders
rubrics_metrics.description: No payment of consideration by the Parent shareholders for SpinCo shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Parent shareholders pay consideration for SpinCo shares the distribution is a 'sale' under the Securities Act and registration is required unless another exemption applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: SLB 4 Condition: Pro rata distribution of SpinCo shares
rubrics_metrics.description: The distribution of SpinCo shares must be pro rata so that Parent shareholders have the same proportionate interest in Parent and SpinCo before and after the spin-off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pro rata is determined by distribution ratio multiplied by number of Parent shares; dual-class voting structures, IPOs or concurrent capital raises can raise issues. Retention of an interest or SpinCo not being wholly-owned does not by itself defeat pro rata if distribution ratios are equal.

rubrics_metrics.name: SLB 4 Condition: Adequate information provided to Parent shareholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent must provide adequate information to its shareholders and to the trading markets about the spin-off to avoid Securities Act registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extent of information depends on Exchange Act reporting status: if both Parent and SpinCo are reporting companies, only transaction-specific info is needed; if Parent is reporting but SpinCo is not, an information statement substantially complying with Reg 14A/14C (business description, risk factors, financials, MD&A) is required; non-reporting Parent must also include transfer limitations designed to prevent a public market in SpinCo prior to Exchange Act registration. SpinCo may be treated as a 'reporting subsidiary' if reporting for at least 90 days and current.

rubrics_metrics.name: SLB 4 Condition: Valid business purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The spin-off must have a valid business purpose (not a shareholder purpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable business purposes include focusing management, enhancing access to financing, resolving shareholder differences, complying with legal decrees, facilitating acquisitions or offerings, cost savings, protecting businesses from risks. A spin-off intended merely to create a market in SpinCo shares without adequate information will fail this test.

rubrics_metrics.name: SLB 4 Condition: Holding period for restricted securities
rubrics_metrics.description: If SpinCo shares are 'restricted securities' (e.g., acquired in a non-public chain of transactions), the Parent must have held the shares for at least two years prior to the spin-off for SLB 4 to be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum notes Rule 144's holding period has since been shortened and suggests it may be appropriate to apply the same shorter holding periods (one year for non-reporting, six months for reporting) to SLB 4, but the Staff has not formally said so. The two-year rule does not apply where Parent formed SpinCo rather than acquiring the business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of relying on SLB 4 for indirect or tax-driven structures
rubrics_metrics.description: SLB 4 applies on its face to spin-offs of 'a subsidiary' but has been applied by Staff in certain indirect demerger structures (e.g., orphan subsidiaries acquiring the business) when tax reasons drive the structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No-action letters are fact-specific and limited to the facts presented; market participants study prior letters closely. If structure is novel or unusual, budget time (one to two months or more) to seek a Staff no-action letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advantages of structuring a spin-off in compliance with SLB 4
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical benefits of satisfying SLB 4 versus registering the distribution under the Securities Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include avoiding registration fees (which can be substantial and are calculated under Rule 457(f)), being subject to a different disclosure liability framework (no strict Section 11 liability for Exchange Act-only registration; instead Rule 10b-5 scienter-based liability), avoiding publicity/gun-jumping restrictions, delayed application of Sarbanes-Oxley until effectiveness of Form 10/20-F (versus public filing of S-1/F-1), and potential to 'inherit' the Parent's reporting history for Form S-3/F-3 and WKSI consideration subject to meeting Item 9 (substantially same assets/segment data) and being current in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditing and auditor independence requirements when registering SpinCo
rubrics_metrics.description: If SpinCo registers under the Securities Act or Exchange Act, its financial statements may need PCAOB auditing and auditors must meet PCAOB and Rule 2-01 of Regulation S-X independence requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm at an early stage that auditors meet PCAOB standards and independence requirements; consider timing and costs of PCAOB audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign private issuer test for SpinCo
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules determining whether SpinCo is a 'foreign private issuer' (FPI) or a 'domestic' issuer for Exchange Act purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If SpinCo is U.S.-incorporated it's domestic. If foreign-incorporated and no more than 50% of outstanding voting securities are held of record by U.S. residents (looking through nominees), SpinCo is an FPI. If >50% will be held by U.S. residents, consider whether a majority of executive officers or directors are U.S. citizens/residents, whether >50% of assets are in U.S., or whether business is principally administered in U.S. The FPI test is run annually and a spin-off can change status; consequences of being domestic include U.S. GAAP, Sarbanes-Oxley quarterly testing, proxy rules, Section 16 short-swing rules, and more detailed compensation disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential submission policies and eligibility (FPI Policy, Section 6(e), 2017 Policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of the SEC's confidential review procedures for draft registration statements and the conditions to rely on each policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FPI Policy is for foreign private issuers and does not require the public filing 15 days prior to effectiveness (unlike 2017 Policy) but requires satisfying one of its conditions: concurrent non-U.S. listing, privatization by foreign government, or conflict with applicable foreign law. Section 6(e) accommodation applies only to Securities Act registration for emerging growth companies. The 2017 Policy covers initial Securities Act registration and Section 12(b) Exchange Act registrations but not voluntary Section 12(g) registrations; thus an SLB 4 spin-off that registers under Section 12(g) would not be eligible under the 2017 Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADR program considerations for Parents with ADRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational, registration and structuring issues when Parent maintains an ADR program and SpinCo will have ADRs or ADSs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether SpinCo ADRs will be sponsored or unsponsored; deposit agreement governs distribution mechanics. ADRs (ADSs) must be registered on Form F-6. Coordination with depositary is critical; depositary receiving SpinCo shares may sell into market and remit cash to shareholders who cannot receive shares. Cash-in-lieu options may be difficult to structure compatibly with U.S. registration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative structuring approaches to avoid U.S. registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Other approaches sometimes considered to address Securities Act registration exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include excluding U.S. shareholders (where legal/commercially practicable), avoiding use of U.S. jurisdictional means, limiting U.S. participants to qualified institutional buyers (Rule 144A) to rely on private placement exemptions (subject to transfer restrictions), or cash-outs for excluded shareholders — each requires careful analysis of home-country law, US jurisdictional contacts, and Staff views (level of U.S. shareholding/trading can affect acceptability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 355/368 tax qualification: Corporate business purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: For tax-free treatment under Sections 355 and 368(a)(1)(D), the spin-off must be motivated by a valid corporate business purpose (not a shareholder purpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business purpose must be material and not achievable in a tax-free manner that is practical and not unduly expensive. Examples of acceptable purposes are listed (focus management, access to financing, antitrust compliance, employee retention, cost savings, protecting businesses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 355/368 tax qualification: Device prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The transaction must not be used as a device for distribution of the Parent's earnings and profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a facts-and-circumstances test; Treasury regulations list factors that cut for or against a finding of device. Careful documentation and structuring required to show spin-off is not a device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 355/368 tax qualification: Control test
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent must have 'control' of SpinCo immediately before the distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control means ownership of at least 80% of combined voting power and 80% of the total number of shares of all other classes. The precise 80% test must be satisfied to qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 355/368 tax qualification: Active trade or business requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately after the distribution, Parent and SpinCo must each be engaged in an active trade or business that was conducted throughout the five-year period preceding the distribution and was not acquired in a taxable transaction during that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'active trade or business' requirement is strict and often a source of foot-faults; diligence on the five-year history and acquisition timing is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 355/368 tax qualification: Continuity of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Historic shareholders of the Parent, as a whole, must maintain a continued interest (generally ~50% ownership) in both Parent and SpinCo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity of interest is measured in value and ownership; structuring must preserve the requisite ownership percentages among historic shareholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 355/368 tax qualification: Continuity of business enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent and SpinCo must continue to operate the businesses post-spin-off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both entities should maintain continuing business operations consistent with the pre-spin-off enterprise; discontinuities can jeopardize tax-free treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 355/368 tax qualification: Permissible entities (limits on certain taxpayers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain entities (e.g., investment corporations, some REITs) are limited in their ability to effect tax-free spin-offs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm entity type eligibility early; statutory and regulatory limitations can preclude tax-free treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 355/368 tax qualification: Anti-avoidance / disguised sale rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Anti-avoidance rules address disguised sales and related transactions that may cause gain recognition despite technical compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disguised sale rules include (i) post-distribution holdings attributable to shares purchased within five years and (ii) Morris Trust-type rules where the distribution is part of a plan that results in acquisition of ≥50% interest; if a disguised sale applies, Parent recognizes gain though shareholders may remain eligible for tax-free treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRS rulings: availability, 'no-rule' areas, and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxpayers can request transactional letter rulings under Rev. Proc. 2017-52, but certain aspects are 'no-rule' areas (business purpose, device, Morris Trust plan) absent a significant novel issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRS is not obligated to rule within a set period (though a pilot 'fast-track' exists for certain spin-offs with a 12-week target under Rev. Proc. 2022-10). The IRS may decline rulings for policy reasons or where issues are under examination/litigation. Decide early whether to seek a ruling or rely on advisor opinion — weighing tax at stake, timeline, and complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent retention of interest: tax and securities consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: When Parent retains an interest in SpinCo, tax considerations typically limit retained interest (often under ~20% for practical reasons) and securities-law consequences (affiliate status) must be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention must not have a principal purpose of avoiding U.S. tax; business purposes for retention (e.g., deleveraging, collateral for financing, employee plans) can justify it. From securities law, retained stakes can make Parent an 'affiliate' with resale restrictions under Rule 144 and other consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposal of retained interest: affiliate/resale rules and registration rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-spin-off sales by Parent of retained SpinCo shares depend on whether Parent is an 'affiliate' (generally ≥10% voting securities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliate resales in the U.S. require registration or reliance on exemptions such as Rule 144 (volume and manner restrictions) or offshore Regulation S (subject to 'substantial U.S. market interest' analysis). Parents often negotiate registration rights with SpinCo to permit future resales (demand or piggyback).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficial ownership reporting: Schedule 13D/13G thresholds and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If SpinCo's shares are registered under Section 12, Parent must report beneficial ownership on Schedule 13D or 13G if beneficial ownership exceeds 5% of a registered class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Parent did not 'acquire' the retained interest post-registration and meets the conditions of Rule 13d-1(d), it may file Schedule 13G within 45 days after year-end; acquisitions that occur after registration may require Schedule 13D unless another exemption applies (qualified institutional investor or passive investor exemptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special listing considerations for SpinCo
rubrics_metrics.description: Listing SpinCo on a U.S. national securities exchange involves particular processes in a spin-off context and may affect governance exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Parent remains listed and retains ≥50% beneficial interest in SpinCo, SpinCo may be exempt from certain listing audit-committee standards under Rule 10A-3(c)(2). Registration via Form 10/Form 20-F differs from typical IPO processes (no separate Form 8-A may be required), and exchanges may seek confirmations from Parent's advisors about listing qualifactions (min share price, number of shareholders, market cap).
